headline: Healthcare and Energy Lead a Broadly Higher Monday as Software Surges on an AI Endorsement
body_html:
Monday's session closed on a constructive note, with 343 stocks advancing against 198 declining across the 544-name universe. Healthcare topped the sector table, gaining 1.82%, while Energy followed closely at 1.78% and Software added 1.57%. The catalyst that arguably set the tone arrived early: a well-known skeptic of Microsoft's artificial-intelligence strategy reversed course publicly, declaring that the company's AI pivot is only in its opening chapter — a signal the market received warmly and that rippled across software names throughout the day.

The standout mover of the session was PTC Inc., which surged 33.49% — a gain of exceptional magnitude for a large industrial-software name. Freight broker RXO Inc. climbed 22.54%, and biotech Genmab added 10.73%, underscoring just how broadly the strength was distributed across unrelated corners of the market. On the other side of the ledger, homebuilders bore the sharpest pain: the group fell 2.02% as a sector, with Lennar sliding 6.73%. Semiconductors also lagged, off 0.72%, as United Microelectronics dropped 8.95% and weighed on the foundry segment.

The split between healthcare and software on one hand, and homebuilders and chips on the other, suggests investors are rotating toward companies with near-term earnings visibility and away from rate-sensitive or cyclically exposed names. With Tuesday's open next on the calendar, traders will be watching whether today's leadership holds or the rotation continues to shuffle.

briefs.headline: PTC Inc. Rockets 33% in a Single Session
briefs.body: PTC Inc. posted the most dramatic single-day gain in the universe on Monday, surging 33.49%. The industrial-software company's move dwarfed every other mover and attracted heavy volume, cementing it as the unambiguous story stock of the session. No other name came close to matching that magnitude.

briefs.headline: Microsoft's AI Repositioning Earns a Prominent Convert
briefs.body: A longtime critic of Microsoft's artificial-intelligence strategy publicly reversed his view Monday, arguing the company's commitment to AI is still in its early stages. The endorsement gave software stocks a visible lift, contributing to the sector's 1.57% gain on the day and lending credibility to the broader AI-infrastructure investment thesis.

briefs.headline: RXO Freight Shares Jump More Than 22%
briefs.body: RXO Inc., the freight brokerage spinoff operating in the industrials sector, surged 22.54% Monday, making it the second-largest gainer in the universe. The move stood out given the broader industrials sector's modest 0.33% advance, suggesting company-specific news rather than sector tailwinds drove the rally.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Bear the Brunt as Lennar Drops Nearly 7%
briefs.body: The homebuilding sector was Monday's clearest loser, falling 2.02% as a group. Lennar led the decline with a 6.73% drop, while the sector's weakness contrasted sharply with the day's otherwise positive tone. Rate sensitivity and affordability concerns continue to weigh on the group's near-term outlook.

briefs.headline: OpenAI Safety Departure Renews Calls for Stricter AI Guardrails
briefs.body: An employee focused on safety at OpenAI resigned and publicly urged regulators to impose nuclear-level oversight on advanced artificial-intelligence systems. The departure adds to a growing chorus of voices inside the industry warning that existing safeguards are inadequate as capabilities accelerate rapidly.

briefs.headline: C.H. Robinson Slides Nearly 11% as Freight Names Diverge
briefs.body: Logistics giant C.H. Robinson fell 10.85% Monday, the steepest percentage decline in the universe, even as crosstown rival RXO surged. The divergence within the freight sector underscored how company-specific factors — rather than macro demand signals — dominated trading across transportation names on the day.
